issue.title: Message board: supervise athena agents through verified completion (2026-09-06)
issue.description:
Purpose and authorization
This is Bryan's explicitly requested proof of concept: use a memory task bead as an append-only message board for a sequential chain of SASE agents supervising all agents running on athena. This is an operational coordination record, not a request to edit a memory file or implement a new bead type. Record evidence about whether a dedicated message-board type would help.

Mission and coverage
Ensure each supervised agent completes its assigned work. Inventory all projects on this machine, not only sase. Track the initial running/waiting/queued agents, any new agents appearing while this chain runs, their continuations and retries, and failed entries whose assigned work remains unresolved. Reconcile historical failure rows with their successful continuations/retries and actual task outcomes before declaring them addressed. Do not resurrect already-completed historical work merely because an old shell or monitor is red. Keep unresolved cases visible; missing artifacts or disappearance from a capped listing are not success evidence.

Cadence and ownership
The setup agent schedules ONE initial monitor running sleep 60. Each successor performs the full checklist below immediately on waking, appends a handoff note, and if work remains schedules sleep 3600 with another successor. Use /sase_monitor; never stay alive polling or promise to resume without a mechanical handoff. Omit --model on these monitors to inherit codex/gpt-6-astra and the starter's reasoning effort. All agents newly launched by this supervision chain, including retries, must use that same model; preserve the assigned task when overriding an older prompt's routing. Do not change healthy existing agents' models.

Ordered check-in procedure
1. Read this entire description and all notes, then capture a fresh machine-wide sase agent list -a -j and sase monitor list --json. Compare per-run evidence with the last checkpoint. Use status_bucket for monitors with custom labels; inspect WAITING and QUEUED causes, runner holders, process liveness, recent transcript/checkpoint progress, and monitored child commands. Long duration or one quiet interval alone is not a stall. Shared-PID plan/code family rows need reconciliation before any kill. Resolve actual blocked dependencies and abandoned continuations. Use /sase_chats for completed chat evidence and sase agent show for details.
2. For a confirmed stall, diagnose and repair the underlying issue when appropriate. Before changing code, inspect repo instructions; use /sase_repo for every other repo, keep shared backend logic in sase-core, and follow verification memory. The user explicitly authorizes committing necessary fixes with /sase_git_commit; use that skill, never git commit. Verify the fix has reached the revision/environment the restarted agent will use. Preview sase agent restart NAME --dry-run before mutation because restart can delete the old artifacts and related runs. Record evidence first, preserve work, target the affected run, and use the same model via -m. Confirm the new live run afterward. A slow but healthy run or a real human gate is not permission to kill it or invent an approval.
3. Investigate each newly failed or still-unresolved failed run. First check for a successful or already-active retry/continuation, including automatic retries, so there is at most one live replacement per failed run. Repair and verify prerequisites and commit necessary fixes as above. Launch an identical task prompt from the stored raw_xprompt.md, changing only identity and the user-required model routing (plus membership adjustments necessary to keep the same task attachment). Explicitly use the id directive and allocate a collision-free child under the failed agent's hood; prefer SASE retry helpers instead of string replacement. Keep bead, workspace, dependency, workflow/finalizer, and clan metadata. Do not silently force same-name reuse for ordinary failed retries. Read /sase_run and relevant xprompt memory when actually launching; this user's retry and monitor authorization persists across the chain. Verify launch admission and the actual retry identity/model rather than treating a queued launch request as a running retry. Track retries through successful task/finalizer completion; a started or failed retry alone never proves recovery. Back off persistent transient errors to the next hourly cycle rather than launching a tight retry storm. Reconcile old-name waiters: a successful child hood name may not automatically satisfy a wait on the failed parent's exact name.
4. Recheck the termination condition using fresh all-project state and the durable ledger. It requires zero remaining running/waiting/queued target agents or active dependent monitors/gates/continuations, and zero failed assignments without a verified successful retry or continuation that completed the same work. Exclude only this supervision family and its own sleep monitor from target counts, to avoid self-perpetuation. Do not count an entire hood or every monitor as excluded. Confirm finalizer/landing outcomes and substantive assigned work, not merely a DONE label. Cover disappearing runs with explicit lookup and saved outcome evidence. The recent list caps completed history at 50 per project; use uncapped sase agent search plus exact identity lookups to detect failures between hourly checks. Establish a final second inventory after reconciliation so races and new launches are not missed. If any uncertainty remains, it remains unresolved and the loop continues.

Handoff protocol
Append notes with sase bead note; do not overwrite other agents' notes. At check-in start record timestamp, supervisor identity, check-in number, predecessor, and scope. Before each restart/retry record the failed run key (project + name + started_at/artifacts_dir), diagnosis, task/prompt source, intended replacement name, and action intent; after it record launch result, actual replacement identity, model, and validation. Each checkpoint must include current running/waiting/queued lists and blockers, per-run progress fingerprints, the failure-to-retry ledger with success evidence or outstanding work, fixes/commit IDs/test results, unresolved questions, and the next monitor action. Preserve evidence needed to distinguish an already-handled failure from a new attempt with the same display name. Record practical message-board strengths/friction as evidence, without launching an unsolicited bead-type implementation.

Monitor invocation and finish
Use the installed CLI help as authoritative. At setup it is: sase monitor start -s SLEEPING -S SLEPT -t 70m -L 'Agent supervision' -r 'Hourly check of supervised agents; see this board' --next '<self-contained instructions including this bead ID and all four steps>' --next-output none -- sleep 3600. The first monitor uses sleep 60 and -t 5m instead. There is no --command flag on this installed version. Omit idle-timeout for intentional sleep. A successful start ends the current turn mechanically; a nonzero start is not a handoff and must be investigated/retried. Each successor must preserve this recurrence and board ID in its own --next, not merely say to check status once.
When the termination condition is actually verified, append a concise final analysis listing required interventions, retry outcomes, exact timestamped evidence supporting zero remaining targets/unresolved failures, and message-board observations. Give the same analysis in the normal final response and invoke /sase_final as the last action before that response. Do not create another monitor then. This board remains a memory-task-shaped experimental log; leaving a terminal note is sufficient and no memory init or actual memory edit is requested.

Record metadata
Owner: Bryan. Supervising family root: 00a. Host: athena. Model: codex/gpt-6-astra (inherit reasoning effort). Initial supervision epoch: 2026-09-06T23:19:30.862435Z. Size: large because the unknown remediation scope may span repositories; this is metadata, not a separate planning/task-worker request. Keep the board open as a coordination record: marking ready would emit an unrelated Memory TaskTriage gate. User-requested message-board semantics take precedence over ordinary memory-correction templating. Never hand-set runtime-owned claimed status.

payload.entry: CHECK-IN 1 START / supervisor 00a--1, predecessor 00a setup + 00a--mon sleep 60, 2026-09-06T23:33:41.058351+00:00. Read the description and baseline note, and captured all-project inventory, complete FAILED catalog, and live/checkpoint evidence. Eight distinct target runner PIDs plus three stale shared-PID plan projections; 29 WAITING, one QUEUED. All eight real target live replies advanced since the setup fingerprints. Initial CLI reads briefly waited on disk I/O (full IO PSI avg10 ~36%, ~25 GiB memory available); they recovered. No evidence of a confirmed agent stall. Zero active monitors at first snapshot. Reconciling historical monitor follow-ups and failure catalog before final checkpoint. No restart, retry, source edit, or commit so far.
